from_node.description: A complex technological system is designed, deployed, operated and governed by many actors whose knowledge and control are distributed.

to_node.description: Because no individual fully controls the system, responsibility disappears into an anonymous technological ordering and cannot be institutionally reassigned or redesigned.

bridge.statement: The problem of many hands is real, but current technology ethics treats institutional design, accountability and meaningful human control as possible responses rather than proof of inevitable responsibilitylessness.

to4.criteria_tradeoffs: control, performance, safety and responsibility can conflict
to4.governance: institutional design can allocate accountability and correction channels
to4.control_responsibility: responsibility must be traced across actual knowledge, control and institutional roles
to4.corrigibility: reversible design choices, review and accountability can increase corrigibility
to4.material_environmental_dependency: organizational and infrastructural embedding affects control
to4.revision_trigger: cases where all meaningful channels of responsibility and control remain structurally absent despite institutional redesign
